solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Maybe wing of hospital is facing the early sun

parts.note: an East Ward is one possible hospital wing, hence 'Maybe'
's is the contraction of is

explanation.surface: A note on hospital design: one wing has its windows catching the sunrise.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'is' as the contraction 's tacked on to the ward's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The early sun rises in the east, so anything turned that way points toward the morning light.

clue.text: Uncanny, the Spanish doctor suppressing skin irritation

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces sit on top of, pressing down on, the last one

parts.note: el is the Spanish masculine article
an itch is an irritation of the skin

explanation.surface: A Spanish doctor eerily keeps a patient's rash under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressing' only places the article and doctor above the itch in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Eldritch describes something weird and unearthly, a literary synonym for uncanny.

clue.text: Rabbit taking vegetable — not rabbit's first

indicators.note: 'not' says the following letter is left out of the vegetable

parts.note: a sprout, the Brussels sprout, is a vegetable

indicators.note: the first letter of the word rabbit's is wanted

parts.note: its first letter is R

explanation.surface: A rabbit nibbles a vegetable, though the vegetable lacks something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' as the definition is the British verb, to rabbit on, meaning to talk at length.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit is British slang for chattering endlessly, and to spout is likewise to talk volubly.

clue.text: Herb goes courting, embracing David North

indicators.note: the courting verb wraps its arms around the next pieces

parts.note: to woo is to court, so 'goes courting' is WOOS
Dave is the short form of David
N is the compass abbreviation for North

explanation.surface: A romantic picture of someone wooing a man called David North with herbs.
explanation.walkthrough: Wood avens is a woodland plant of the rose family, also called herb bennet.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood avens is a wild plant traditionally used in medicine, classed among the herbs.

clue.text: Are singers in Queen film to get back in Top Twenty?

definitions.text: to get back in Top Twenty

parts.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

indicators.note: the charring word goes inside the film title

parts.note: ET is the Spielberg film
things that char are singeing things, so they are 'singers'

explanation.surface: Asks whether a Queen biopic's soundtrack could put the band back in the pop charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are singers' is the trick: not vocalists, but ones that singe, which is what charring does.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-chart is for a record to re-enter the hit parade, getting a place in the best-sellers list once more.

clue.text: Bar quite regularly brought in offer to buy a round

indicators.note: the alternate letters are brought inside the pub word

parts.note: a shout is a turn to buy drinks, in Australian and British pub slang

indicators.note: taking every other letter of quite

parts.note: its second and fourth letters, read alternately, are U and T

explanation.surface: In a bar, someone fairly often offers to buy the next round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: A shout is a turn to buy everyone's drinks, as in 'my shout'.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut out is to exclude or keep away, the verb sense of barring someone.

clue.text: Quarrel about right fish

indicators.note: the quarrel goes around the next letter

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: Two people argue over the proper fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The sprat is a small silvery sea creature of the herring family.

clue.text: Thus regularly take to cook in marinade

parts.note: so means thus, in that way
to use a drug is to take it habitually

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction about routinely marinating the food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like the alternate-letters signal, but here it belongs with 'take' as a phrase meaning use.
explanation.definitionFit: To souse is to steep food such as herring in pickle or vinegar.

clue.text: Control plane over top of errant balloon again

indicators.note: in a down clue the control word sits over what follows

parts.note: to rein in is to control
a plane is a flat, level surface

indicators.note: the first letter, at the top in a down entry

parts.note: its first letter is E

explanation.surface: Someone steers a plane over a stray balloon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft, but it is the geometric sense of a level surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To balloon is to swell up, so to do it again is to blow up with air a second time.

clue.text: Angry speech one used in exchange

indicators.note: the numeral is placed inside the exchange word

parts.note: trade is exchange of goods
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper in an exchange of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long, furious outburst of words directed at someone.

clue.text: Two people taking month for construction in Italy

parts.note: a duo is a pair of people

explanation.surface: A couple spend a month on some building project in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Duomo is Italian for cathedral, a grand building such as the one in Florence.

clue.text: Physicist holding out to get Rutherford's head designer

indicators.note: the physicist's name holds the next word inside it

parts.note: Marie or Pierre Curie, the physicists

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter is R

explanation.surface: A physicist stubbornly holds out to win Rutherford's backing for a design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is taken as written, held inside the physicist's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A couturier creates and makes fashionable clothes, a designer of haute couture.

clue.text: Popular jazz style introducing a prelude

indicators.note: the jazz pieces come first, introducing the final letter

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
trad is traditional jazz

explanation.surface: A popular type of jazz used as an opening number.
explanation.walkthrough: Trad is short for traditional jazz, the revival New Orleans style popular in 1950s Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An intrada is an introductory piece of music, an overture or opening movement.

clue.text: Terminated agent having taken a lot in

parts.note: something that has terminated is over
a fed is a US federal agent

explanation.surface: An agent who has been fired after letting a lot slip in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terminated agent' reads like a sacked spy; it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Overfed describes someone given too much to eat, who has consumed a large quantity.

clue.text: Inn may have done this ordering a red table-cloth

definitions.note: past participle phrase: an Inn of Court has done it to a student

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A pub's landlord orders a red tablecloth.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Inn' is not a pub but one of London's Inns of Court, such as Gray's Inn, which admit barristers.
explanation.definitionFit: Inns of Court formally admit students to practise as barristers, a ceremony known by this phrase.

clue.text: Nature of theft is so unclear, unfortunately

definitions.note: adjective: having the nature of theft

indicators.note: an unfortunate arrangement of letters signals they are mixed up

explanation.surface: A regretful remark that it is uncertain whether a crime was a theft.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is the legal term for stealing, so a larcenous act partakes of thieving.

clue.text: One's sent off for this description of Aquae Sulis?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sports player sent off goes for an ...
second meaning: Aquae Sulis was the Roman name of the city of Bath, an ancient Bath

explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English city whose Roman name was Aquae Sulis; in football a player sent off is said to have an early bath.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for leaving the field prematurely, and literally the Roman-era version of the spa city.

clue.text: Witness a time trial with stripped-down Ford

parts.note: a test is a trial

indicators.note: stripped of its outer letters, leaving the middle

parts.note: its middle letters are OR

explanation.surface: A witness to a time trial in a stripped-down Ford car.
explanation.definitionFit: An attestor vouches for or certifies something, like one who signs as a witness.

clue.text: Tense and concise statement of Pollyanna's views?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the grammatical tense of 'I have done'
second meaning: Pollyanna, the relentless optimist, thinks the present is perfect

explanation.walkthrough: Pollyanna is the heroine of a children's novel who always finds something to be glad about.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb form for completed actions with present relevance, and an optimist's summary of now.

clue.text: Sweetheart's in resetting bones for some cosmetic surgery

indicators.note: the sweetheart goes inside the rearranged letters
setting the letters again in a new order

parts.note: Jo is an old Scots word for a sweetheart

explanation.surface: A darling is in surgery having bones reset during a cosmetic procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resetting' acts on 'bones' to give NOSEB; JO goes inside that, after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinoplasty, reshaping the nose, is a common cosmetic operation known informally by this name.

clue.text: Solo dance is out of fashion you feel at the end

parts.note: passé means outdated

indicators.note: take the final letter of each of these words

parts.note: its last letter is U
its last letter is L

explanation.surface: A dancer worries that solo dancing is out of fashion, as one feels in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Pas seul is the ballet term for a dance performed by one person.

clue.text: More immediate Conservative failure

parts.note: a loser is a failure

explanation.surface: A Tory loss seems more pressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nearer, in time or relation, is more direct and immediate.

clue.text: Scenery material overturned — the cause of Hamlet's death

indicators.note: turned over, so the pieces read from the end back

parts.note: a set is stage scenery
material means real, physical

explanation.surface: Stage scenery topples during a Hamlet production, killing the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's play Laertes kills Hamlet with a poisoned rapier in the final duel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophelia's brother wounds the prince with a venom-tipped sword in their fencing match.

clue.text: Ends with boy finally drunk

parts.note: tips are ends

indicators.note: 'finally' means at the very end, so only the closing letter of boy is used

parts.note: its final letter is Y

explanation.surface: A boy ends up drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipsy means slightly intoxicated.

clue.text: What's bad for PC behaviour? Pray we and society reform

indicators.note: to re-form the letters is to shape them anew

explanation.surface: A plea for society to reform behaviour that falls short of political correctness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PC' suggests political correctness, but it is a personal computer. S for society goes in front of the rearranged PRAY WE.
explanation.definitionFit: Spyware is malicious software that covertly monitors a computer and harms how it runs.

clue.text: Italian region mostly down by river is humming

indicators.note: reduced by, so the next letter is removed
'mostly' means most but not all of it, so the region's name loses its closing letter

parts.note: Abruzzo is a region of central Italy

explanation.surface: An Italian region, mostly downriver, busy with activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of ABRUZZO to give ABRUZZ, then 'down by river' means less R.
explanation.definitionFit: Abuzz describes a place full of activity and noise, as with buzzing.

clue.text: Joys people mostly somehow got in casual wear

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged in some way
all but the last letter, dropping the final E

explanation.surface: Joyful people somehow got dressed in relaxed clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: A sloppy joe is a loose, baggy sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloppy joe is a loose, baggy sweater, comfortable informal clothing.

clue.text: A day in the last month of age

parts.note: ult., ultimo, means of last month in old business letters

explanation.surface: Coming of age falls on a day last month.
explanation.walkthrough: Ult. (ultimo) is an old commercial abbreviation for last month.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has come of age is legally grown up.

clue.text: Reliable? It doesn't start, impaired by neglect

indicators.note: the word loses its starting letter

parts.note: trusty means reliable

explanation.surface: A trusty old car that won't start after being neglected.
explanation.definitionFit: Skills or metal left unused grow rusty, deteriorating through lack of use.

clue.text: Large bottle's risk after spicy dish? Finish off both

indicators.note: the risk comes after the dish
to finish off something here is to take away its finishing letter

parts.note: a balti is a spicy curry dish

indicators.note: 'both' applies the same trimming to the risk word as well

parts.note: hazard means risk

explanation.surface: A big bottle risks being served after a curry, finishing off both.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish off both' trims the last letter from BALTI and from HAZARD. A balti is a curry served in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A balthazar is an outsize champagne bottle holding twelve standard bottles.
